rationale: Baseline sparse lexical model using word TF-IDF and one-vs-rest Logistic Regression.
interpretation: This sets the first Hamming Loss benchmark using exact-word and phrase evidence.

rationale: Adds text cleanup, a source Type token, stricter document frequency limits, and longer word n-grams.
interpretation: This tests whether source metadata and cleaner phrase features improve the baseline.

rationale: Uses a margin-based Linear SVM with balanced class weights on word TF-IDF features.
interpretation: This tests whether a large-margin classifier handles sparse SDG indicator language better than Logistic Regression.

rationale: Combines word and character TF-IDF features with class-balanced Logistic Regression.
interpretation: Character n-grams should help with acronyms, noisy wording, and rare health indicator phrasing.

rationale: Uses pretrained MiniLM sentence embeddings with one-vs-rest Logistic Regression.
interpretation: This tests semantic representation against sparse lexical TF-IDF features.

rationale: Uses MiniLM sentence embeddings with a Classifier Chain ordered by label frequency.
interpretation: This tests whether modeling label dependencies improves multi-label predictions.

rationale: Tunes per-label thresholds for the strongest probability-based TF-IDF model.
interpretation: This directly optimizes the assignment metric because Hamming Loss depends on binary label decisions.

rationale: Combines the best sparse TF-IDF signal with MiniLM semantic embeddings.
interpretation: This tests whether lexical phrase matching and semantic similarity make complementary errors.
